[38956] 2026-11 - A-2025-92957 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
item.description: I am requesting copies of records held by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), specifically records held by the Digital Strategy, Services and Innovation Sector (DSSIS), relating to monitoring, management oversight, compliance, and audit activities associated with GCMS, Chinook (including Chinook+), and other application processing technologies used to support immigration processing. I request the following final records created or used by DSSIS during this period: Reports and dashboards used to monitor operational performance, integrity, and compliance in relation to GCMS, Chinook/Chinook+, and other application processing technologies (e.g., performance monitoring, incident reporting, error reporting, adoption/use reporting). Audits, evaluations, reviews or assessments (including post-implementation reviews and lessons-learned reports) relating to GCMS, Chinook/Chinook+, and other application processing technologies, including any findings and recommendations regarding oversight, governance, compliance or management issues. Any DSSIS records (briefing notes, deck summaries, governance memos) describing audit trail / traceability features and management monitoring mechanisms used for these technologies (e.g., session-based tracking, tagging, metrics definitions, retention policies at a high level). I am not requesting raw system logs, databases, or personal employee information. Where records contain personal information, please sever as required under the Act. If any part of this request is considered too broad, please advise what scope refinement would allow retrieval of the most relevant oversight records with minimal delay. Remove duplicate copies of documents and emails. Only provide the final copy or the latest draft of a document. Only provide you with the final email in a chain of emails. Mark all Cabinet Confidences as non-relevant. Only provide records are sent to and or by an individual at the EX minus 1 level or higher (middle manager level). (From 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31). | 67 pages | Source: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada

item.title: [38956] 2026-11 - A-2026-35897 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
item.description: I am writing to request records under the Access to Information Act relating to the Start-Up Visa (SUV) Program, for the period January 1, 2020 to the 2026-07-24. To ensure clarity and facilitate processing, I have attached a spreadsheet template illustrating the structure and data fields requested. The spreadsheet is provided as a guide only and reflects the categories described below. Purpose of Year-of-Filing Comparison This request seeks a year-by-year breakdown to permit comparison among applications filed in the same calendar year. In particular, the requested data will identify, for each designated organization and for each filing year, how many Start-Up Visa applications from that cohort have received a final decision (approval or refusal) and how many remain undecided. This information is requested to assess whether applications from the same filing cohort have generally been processed while others remain outstanding. Scope of Request For all Start-Up Visa permanent residence applications, broken down by designated organization, please provide the following information: 1. Applications Received Total number of Start-Up Visa applications received by IRCC Shown: by calendar year (2020 onward), and cumulatively Broken down by designated organization 2. Applications In Process (No Final Decision) Number of applications currently in process with no final decision Including: applications with an assigned GCMS file number, and applications received but not yet assigned a file number, if tracked Shown: by calendar year of receipt, and cumulatively Broken down by designated organization 3. Applications Finalized Decisions Rendered For applications with a final decision: Number of approved applications Number of refused applications Shown: by calendar year of decision, and cumulatively Broken down by designated organization 4. Definitions / Notes Any internal definitions used for: application received in process approved refused Any known limitations or qualifications affecting the data (e.g., delays between receipt and GCMS file creation) If any portion of this request is unclear or overly broad, I would appreciate the opportunity to clarify or refine it. (From: 2020-01-01 To: 2026-07-24). | 154 pages | Source: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada

item.title: [38956] 2026-11 - A-2025-20815 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
item.description: As per Supplementary Information for the 2025-2027 Immigration Levels Plan dated October 24, 2024, IRCC released immigrant admission levels for various categories. Once such category is the In-Canada Focus Category. As per subnote #6, it includes "Primarily admissions from the Canadian Experience Class and other regional immigration pathways but may also come from Federal Skilled Workers and Federal Skilled Trades". Total targeted admissions in this category are 82,980. As of May 19, 2025, IRCC only invited 9850 candidates under the In-Canada Focus Category which is primarily from the Canadian Experience Class as tracked from the Express Entry Rounds of Invitations in the year 2025. Allocations to the regional immigration pathways cannot be tracked. For Candidates to have a better understanding of the allocations under the In-Canada Focus Category, please share the following information: 1) Name of all regional immigration pathways included in this category 2) Total Year to date allocations for the year 2025 3) Year to date allocations breakdown by stream for the year 2025 namely the Canadian Experience Class, Federal Skilled Workers, Federal Skilled Trades and all other regional immigration pathways. 4) What is the range of CRS candidates in the pool can expect for the remaining 2025 5) Any other Ministerial instructions, emails, notes, briefing shared within the IRCC related to #1, #2, #3 and #4. Hoping for a clear view of the allocations for the In-Canada Focus Category for the year 2025. Remove duplicate copies of documents and emails. (From 2025-01-01 to 2025-05-19). | 84 pages | Source: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada

item.description: From January 1, 2025, to present, March 17, 2026 please provide records held by IRCC relating to the interpretation and application of IRPR R188(1)(c) short-term study exemption (course/program of study of 6 months or less completed within the period authorized upon entry) and its interaction with: 1. extensions/changes of status from within Canada (e.g., visitor record extension, work permit issuance/extension including PGWP, maintained status); and 2. distance learning/online study completed while physically in Canada, including programs that have an in-Canada component (exams/labs/practicums/placements). Records requested include (but are not limited to): briefing notes, internal Q&As, decks, policy interpretation notes, implementation notes, stakeholder communications, and internal correspondence with substantive discussion. Please include records connected to the update reflected on the PDI page Study permits: Who needs a study permit and any related efforts to align public webpages/Help Centre answers with Program Delivery Instructions.
